issues.situation: The rule books an overwatch cost that the 11e engine never applies. Every bench game runs at edition 11 (--bench-11e, --bench-difficulty=3). In base 5e70bc2, 40k/phases/ChargePhase.gd resolves no Fire Overwatch against a declared charge and logs '[11e 15.08] no Fire Overwatch against charging ...'. FIRE OVERWATCH (fire_overwatch_11e) is offered only at the end of the opponent's Movement phase, so it is already over when the charge decision is made. A TITANIC unit can never use it (StratagemManager.fire_overwatch_shooter_reason_11e). The local V9-era bench logs show this line 29 times and 0 overwatch offers in the charge phase. So lo_fail_ow = (1-p) x ow_risk.expected_damage subtracts a phantom cost. The design fixes s7467 only through that term: without it, score 1.60 clears the 1.0 bar. On the bench lists, _estimate_overwatch_risk has no TITANIC or timing check, so the enemy Stompa sets the number. Porting it to the fixture saves gives 4.4 dmg vs Stormboyz, 6.5 vs Wazdakka, 9.1 vs Warbikers and 11.0-11.3 vs Wartrikes and Mek in the Orks mirror, and 5.7-6.8 vs every Custodes unit in asym. In round 2 of the Orks mirror, and in the asym arm where the candidate plays Custodes, a charge needing 9+ into a cheaper-per-wound unit within 24" of the enemy Stompa must then score about 4-11 (Orks) or 5-7 (Custodes). The base has already multiplied that same score by 0.1-0.32 for the same phantom overwatch. Such charges are therefore dropped almost every time. This is a large change to round-2 Ork charging with no measured support. The only Orks-mirror low-odds guardrail (s7408 r3, Stormboyz to Zodgrod 8%) leans toward charging (-5.08). The design's own first draft dropped it, and only the round gate protects it; nothing protects the same charge in round 2.
issues.proposed_change: Drop the design. The minimum correct change is to remove the failed-roll overwatch term when GameConstants.edition >= 11, or at least exclude TITANIC, engaged and battle-shocked shooters from _estimate_overwatch_risk. With that change s7467 is no longer dropped (1.60 >= 1.0), so the rule fixes no finding. A sound replacement must price a real 11e cost of a SUCCESSFUL charge. Examples: the engaged charger loses snap shooting, Heroic Intervention and its next Shooting phase; it can be locked with a target it cannot kill (s7467 A: locked with Battlewagon Alpha); and CP is spent re-rolling a 9+ charge. Any replacement must also be checked on the bench lists (Speedwaaagh Orks and the bench Custodes list), not only on custodes_lions and Orks_2000.

issues.situation: The trade gate (points-per-wound ratio < 1) does not mean 'elite charging cheap' on the bench lists, so the guardrail checks do not carry over. The design marks s7431, s7433 and s7452 as 'consistent: trade up'. But Allarus into Custodian Guard is x1.07 in custodes_lions and x0.78 in mirror_custodes_2000 (275 pts/20 W = 13.75 vs 215/20 = 10.75). UNLEASH THE LIONS (CustodesCodexOther._unleash_apply) copies meta.points = 275 into each one-model Allarus. After the round-2 split each model has 68.75 ppw and trades down into every target. Guard D-F (225 pts) into Guard A-C (215 pts), and Prosecutors into Guard A-C, also count as trading down by 4%. I replayed the rule's test on local Custodes-mirror bench records. In 60 V5 games it drops 6 of 130 low-odds declarations: 5 are single Allarus models into Custodian Guard Gamma (scores 0.5-1.3) and 1 is Prosecutors into Guard Gamma. In 4 V9-era games it drops 2: Prosecutors into Guard Gamma at 17%, score 1.1. The measured critic cases most like Allarus into Guard at 17% (s7431 r2 -5.08, s7452 r2 -1.67) lean toward charging.
issues.proposed_change: Require a margin, e.g. trade < 0.95. That still covers s7467 (0.92) and removes the 4% artifacts. Compute ppw for split units as points x models_now / models_at_start. Re-run the guardrail checks with the bench fixture lists.

issues.situation: The design fixes 1 of the 3 findings. s7469 is untouched: Stormboyz at 14 ppw into a Blade Champion at 25 ppw is a trade up. s7457, added after the designers started, is also untouched: 3 Prosecutors at 15 ppw into a 1-model Prosecutor Squad at 45 ppw is x1.3, a trade up. The report does not check s7457.
issues.proposed_change: Report the coverage as 1 of 3. Do not count s7457 or s7469 as addressed.

issues.situation: The movement phase still plans these charges. The phase plan keeps charge_intent for long charges (a post-move distance over 9" only halves the intent score). It blends 70% of the move toward the charge target and skips firing-position preservation and half-range moves. When CH-LOW-ODDS then refuses the charge, that move bought nothing. A one-round rollout that starts at the charge decision cannot see this, because both branches share the move. In full games it happens every time the rule fires.
issues.proposed_change: Apply the same CH-LOW-ODDS test when charge_intent is built in rounds 1-2, and drop the intent when the post-move charge would be refused. The unit then keeps its firing lane or objective move.

issues.situation: The bar is a fixed 1.0. It ignores the tempo reduction the AI applies when it is behind on VP. At Competitive the un-lowered bar is actually 0.7 (difficulty x0.7). Below Competitive, _get_trade_efficiency returns 1.0, so the rule never fires for Hard or Normal opponents. The bench runs at Competitive, so it does fire there.
issues.proposed_change: Use the bar the AI would use in round 3 (charge_threshold divided by the round-strategy factor) instead of a constant, and state the difficulty gate.

issues.situation: The report's firing evidence comes from the critic lists (Orks_2000 with Lootas, and custodes_lions), not from the bench lists. Its claim 'in mirrors it rarely fires (trade ~1)' is false for the bench Orks mirror, where Speedwaaagh ppw spans 4.1-20 and the Stompa dominates the overwatch term. The s7469 count ('3 distinct drops in P1's r2 charge phase after the decision') cannot be right. After a P2 round-2 decision, P1's next charge phase is in round 3, which the round gate excludes.
issues.proposed_change: Re-count firing on the three bench fixtures (mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy, mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy, asym_2000_postdeploy) before any bundle run.

reviews.fires_in_bench: It will fire in the bench, so it is not a no-op, but most of that firing falls outside the measured evidence. The bench runs at Competitive, so the trade gate is active. (1) Custodes mirror: about 0.1-0.5 changed charge declarations per game, measured by replaying the rule's test on local bench records: 6 in 60 V5 games, 2 in 4 V9-era games. These are single Allarus models after the round-2 split, and Prosecutors, making long charges into Custodian Guard with scores of 0.5-1.3. Custodes snap-shot damage is only 0.4-0.7, so here the rule acts as a raised bar (~1.4-1.6) rather than an overwatch cost. (2) Orks mirror: an estimated 0.5-3 per game; there are no local Orks-mirror records, so this is unverified. The enemy Stompa's estimate (4.4-11.3 dmg) sets a bar of 4-11. Stormboyz, Warbikers, Wartrikes, Mek, Wazdakka and Stompa all trade down into most Speedwaaagh units, so nearly every round-1/2 charge at 28% or less within 24" of the enemy Stompa is dropped. (3) Asym: an estimated 0.5-1.5 per game in the arm where the candidate plays Custodes. Custodes units, and every split Allarus at 68.75 ppw, face Stompa estimates of 5.7-6.8 and a bar of 5-7. The rule rarely fires in the arm where the candidate plays Orks. Most bench firing comes from a TITANIC Stompa that can never Fire Overwatch, at a moment when the engine resolves no overwatch.
reviews.strengths: The change is small, local (one block in _evaluate_best_charge) and behind a parameter. FIX_CHARGE_LOW_ODDS=0 skips the block and restores base behaviour. A dropped target carries score 0 into _score_multi_target_combo (value_if = score/p), so it cannot return through a multi-target declaration. It does not depend on keeper logic, plans or other FIX_ params, and does not affect rounds 3-5. It leaves the harmful guardrail s7470 (Stormboyz trade up) and all round-3 guardrails unchanged. In the critic Custodes-vs-Orks_2000 matchup, the low-odds charges it would flip lean its way: s7467 +2.64 (clear), s7438 +4.75, s7437 Guard to Mek +2.17, s7417 +1.17, s7473 -2.42. Mean is +1.66 VP per flip, though most are not significant. It does fire in the bench, so a benchmark can detect an effect.
reviews.summary: Read from origin/claude/awesome-clarke-31p54m, commit a554ad1; it is not in the local tree. The rule drops round-1/2 charges under 30% when the charger trades down on points per wound and score - (1-p) x overwatch < 1.0. Its stated mechanism, overwatch eaten on a failed roll, is a 10th-edition rule. In this 11e engine a charge declaration draws no Fire Overwatch, which happens at the end of the opponent's Movement phase, and TITANIC units can never use it. So the rule fixes its one finding (s7467) only through a phantom term. It misses s7469 and the later finding s7457: both are trade-ups, and s7457 is x1.3 (3 Prosecutors at 15 ppw into a 1-model squad at 45 ppw). On the bench lists the proxy points at different units than in the evidence. The Speedwaaagh Stompa's estimate (4.4-11.3 dmg) makes the rule drop almost every round-2 long charge into a cheaper unit in the Orks mirror. In asym it does the same for Custodes charges, including every split Allarus, whose copied 275-pt meta gives it 68.75 ppw. The Orks-mirror change has no measured support, and the one Orks-mirror guardrail leans toward charging. In the Custodes mirror it fires about 0.1-0.5 times per game, through ppw artifacts. The other costs are minor: refused charges waste the movement planned for them, and the fixed 1.0 bar ignores tempo. Removing the phantom term is the minimum fix, but then the design fixes nothing, so the verdict is drop. A sound narrow rule would need to price a real 11e cost of a successful charge: the engaged unit loses snap shooting, Heroic Intervention and its next Shooting phase, can be locked with a target it cannot kill, and spends CP re-rolling a 9+ charge. It must also be checked on the bench lists. Reproduction scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/ (ow_port.py, ow_port_notitanic.py, scan_bench.py, scan_logs.py, units.py, decode_save.py).

issues.situation: The cost that decides the rule never happens in the game. CH-LOW-ODDS subtracts lo_fail_ow = (1-p) x ow_risk.expected_damage, which it calls the overwatch a unit takes when its charge roll fails. The engine plays 11e (AIBenchmarkRunner sets GameConstants.edition = 11, and rollouts use the same runner). At 11e no unit can Fire Overwatch at a charging unit. In ChargePhase.gd, the edition >= 11 branch (lines ~607-611) only logs '[11e 15.08] no Fire Overwatch against charging %s (it is used at the end of the opponent's Movement phase)'. StratagemManager.gd fire_overwatch_11e (lines ~5070-5090) can only be used in the movement_phase_end window, and never by a TITANIC unit. The archived 11e bench logs (bench_data/ai_versions_11e_2026-10-29/_logs) show 11-15 such lines per game and no overwatch offers in the Charge phase. The one finding the design fixes, s7467, depends only on this term: the score is 1.60 and the bar is 1.0, so the charge passes without the term. With the term, 1.60 - 0.83 x 7.22 is about -4.4, so the charge is dropped. In the bench the term mostly comes from the Ork Stompa, a TITANIC unit that cannot Fire Overwatch at all. _estimate_overwatch_risk does not check TITANIC, so it estimates 4.4-11.3 damage against Ork units and 4.6-5.5 against Custodes. That raises the bar to about 4-11.
issues.proposed_change: Do not ship this design. Taking out the made-up overwatch term leaves s7467 unchanged (1.60 >= 1.0), so the design would change no finding. A narrow rule that is worth keeping must use a cost the 11e engine really applies, then be measured again. Examples: the unit is locked in a poor fight when the charge succeeds, CP is spent on Fury of the Emperor or a re-roll, or the unit can no longer use Fire Overwatch or Heroic Intervention next turn. Separately, _estimate_overwatch_risk should return 0 at edition >= 11 and should skip TITANIC shooters. That is an existing bug in the base AI, but this design relies on it more heavily.

issues.situation: The design fixes 1 of the 3 findings. F1 (s7469): the Stormboyz are 140 pts for 10 models, 14.0 points per wound. Blade Champion Alpha is 25.0 points per wound, so the trade is x1.30 and the charge is unchanged. The designer's report says this. F3 (s7457): the P2 Prosecutors have 3 models alive, 15.0 points per wound. The P1 Prosecutor squad they charge has 1 model alive, 45.0 points per wound, so the trade is x1.30 and the 8% charge is unchanged. The report does not check F3; it was added after the designers started.
issues.proposed_change: Add F3 to decision_checks and record it as not fixed, so the judge sees 1/3 instead of 1/2.

issues.situation: The trade check 'trades down' has no margin, so almost-equal units fall on either side by chance. In the bench Custodes mirror, Custodian Guard D/E/F (225 pts, 11.25 points per wound) charging Guard A/B/C (10.75) gives a trade of 0.956 and counts as trading down. In the other direction it does not count. In asym, Allarus into Stormboyz is 0.945. At s7473, Lootas Gamma (0.74) is dropped, but Burna Boyz Beta (exactly 1.00) stays. Points per wound also rises as models die, so a damaged charger is treated as trading down.
issues.proposed_change: If any form of this rule is kept, require a real gap, for example trade < 0.85.

issues.situation: A position that leaned the other way was not replayed. s7473 r2 P2 (neutral, -2.42 [-6.82, +1.98], n=12, leans toward charging being right): Allarus charge at Lootas Gamma 8% + Burna Boyz Beta. The Allarus to Lootas C trade is 0.74 and the estimated overwatch is 7.22 (Lootas A), so Lootas Gamma is dropped from the declared multi-target charge. This moves the AI toward the option that measured worse.
issues.proposed_change: Replay s7473 r2 and report it with the guardrails.

issues.situation: The bar of 1.0 is called 'the un-lowered bar', but it is not. At Competitive, the threshold without the round-1/2 cut is 1.0 x 0.7 (difficulty) = 0.7, and 0.47 / 0.58 in round 3 with Custodes / Ork aggression. So the rule asks for more than round 3 itself does. The code comment says the Ork cut is '/1.8'; FACTION_AGGRESSION_ORKS is now 1.2.
issues.proposed_change: Compute the bar as the real threshold without STRATEGY_EARLY_CHARGE, and fix the comment.

issues.situation: The test pins the made-up mechanic. The finding-shape test works only because a 5-model Deffgun unit is within 24" and the defender has CP 3. The fixture defines _finding_snapshot(with_shooter=false), but no test uses it, so nothing shows that the overwatch term decides the result. Otherwise the test is good: it drives _decide_charge, pins the fix on, erases the override, and fails on the base because the base declares the charge. It also sets _current_difficulty and does not restore it; this is harmless in a -s run.
issues.proposed_change: If the design is reworked, base the test on the real cost, and add a case without the shooter.

issues.situation: The rule does nothing below Competitive: _get_trade_efficiency returns 1.0 when use_trade_analysis is false. The bench runs Competitive (ai_versions.py run defaults --difficulty 3), so the bench is not affected, but player games at Normal or Hard never see the fix. Corner case: a dropped target stays in scored_targets with score 0. A multi-target combo that includes it ties the single-target EV, and the strict '>' normally blocks the combo, but a float rounding error could let a declaration that lists the dropped target win.
issues.proposed_change: Leave dropped targets out of _evaluate_multi_target_charge, and state that the rule applies at Competitive only.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
My estimate is that it fires often in both Ork fixtures and sometimes in the Custodes mirror. Almost all of it comes from the overwatch term that never happens in the game. I worked this out from the code and fixture data; I did not run Godot. The bench runs at Competitive, so the trade check is active. Points per wound and estimated overwatch come from the fixture saves.

(1) Custodes mirror. The only overwatch estimate is 0.2-0.7 (1.5 against Prosecutors), so the bar is about 1.2-1.6. Only some pairs trade down: Guard D/E/F into Guard A/B/C at 0.956, Allarus into Guard or Prosecutors at 0.78-0.82, Blade Champions into most units, and more pairs after casualties. I re-scored the 3 archived 11e Custodes-mirror bench logs (older AI, units at full strength). It fires in 1 of 3 games: 9 log lines, 3 distinct dropped targets, and one declared multi-target charge loses a target. So expect it in about 1/3 of games, with at most 1 changed declaration per game.

(2) Ork mirror. The enemy Stompa is estimated at 4.4-11.3 overwatch damage against every Ork unit within 24". The Stompa, Wazdakka, Stormboyz, Mek and Wartrikes trade down into cheaper units. The bar becomes about 4-11, so almost every round 1-2 charge under 30% that trades down near the Stompa is dropped. Expect it in most games, in both seats, with about 1-3 changed declarations per game.

(3) Asym. Custodes chargers face an estimated 4.6-5.5 from the Stompa (bar about 4.3-6.1). Allarus and Blade Champions trade down into nearly every Ork unit, and Guard into the cheap ones. So most round 1-2 Custodes long-shot charges within 24\" of the Stompa are dropped. Ork Stormboyz or a Mek charging Guard or Prosecutors face at most 1.7 (bar about 1.4-2.6) and are dropped some of the time.

The bench pairs will not be identical, so a difference can show. But that difference comes from overwatch by a TITANIC unit, which cannot Fire Overwatch, in an edition that has no overwatch against charges.
reviews.strengths: The change is small and every changed path is gated. All new code sits inside 'if get_param(FIX_CHARGE_LOW_ODDS) > 0.0 and ...', and GDScript stops evaluating at the first false condition, so 0 gives exactly the base behaviour. The only other changes are the new constants. It is cheap: the two _get_trade_efficiency calls run only after the cheap checks on chance and round pass. Decision records stay consistent: the ch_low_odds term keeps sum(terms) == score, dropped targets show 0 in the no-charge record, and they add 0 to multi-target EV. It adds a new [CHARGE_LOW_ODDS] log line and removes none. It does not depend on the keeper release. The test drives the real _decide_charge path, pins the fix on and erases the override, and fails on the base for the right reason. Its claimed results agree with the code: s7467 is dropped (trade 0.92, estimated overwatch 7.22, matching the report's 7.2). s7469 and the key harmful guardrail s7470 are unchanged because Stormboyz into Blade Champions is x1.30, so s7470 is still a charge, which is correct. The round-3 guardrails (s7431, s7403, s7441, s7408) are skipped by the round check, and s7431 r2, s7433 r2 and s7454 r2 trade up.
reviews.summary: DROP. The rule drops a round 1-2 charge under 30% by a unit that trades down unless score - (1-p) x estimated overwatch >= 1.0. Its premise is that a failed charge still takes overwatch. In this engine at 11e, which is what the bench and the rollouts play, nothing fires overwatch at a declared charge: ChargePhase logs '[11e 15.08] no Fire Overwatch against charging ...', and Fire Overwatch is offered only at the end of the opponent's Movement phase, never to TITANIC units. So the deciding term is made up. It is the only reason s7467 changes: 1.60 clears the 1.0 bar without the term. F1 (s7469) and the late-added F3 (s7457) do not change, because both chargers trade up (x1.30). That makes 1 of 3 findings fixed. In the bench, the rule's effect would come mostly from the Ork Stompa's estimated 4-11 damage of overwatch, which is impossible. Through that it would block most early long-shot charges in the Ork mirror and on the Custodes side of asym, without measured support (Ork-mirror charge positions are neutral). Smaller problems: the trade check has no margin, so units of near-equal value fall either way. The 1.0 bar is above the real round-3 bar. s7473, which leans toward charging being right, was not replayed and would change. The test drives the real decision path correctly but encodes the overwatch mechanic that does not exist. Fixing the term would make the design change no finding, so drop it. A narrow rule here needs a cost the engine really applies, such as the success-branch lock-in or the CP spent. Evidence: ChargePhase.gd and StratagemManager.gd in /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/40k, and the archived 11e logs in /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/bench_data/ai_versions_11e_2026-10-29/_logs. The design files are not in the working tree; I read them from commit a554ad1.

issues.situation: CLO-CARRIER contradicts how this engine resolves melee, and the s7469 flip depends on it. Custodes vs Orks_2000 (critic list) games affect every Kommandos and Stormboyz fight. When no model's resolved loadout carries the weapon the AI assigns, RulesEngine._melee_weapon_swingers falls back to ALL eligible models. FightPhase._validate_assign_attacks only checks that the weapon exists and is melee. For the Kommandos, _auto_assign_unassigned_models_for_unit then also gap-fills Choppas on top. Engine logs confirm this: 'Kommandos (Big Choppa) -> Allarus Custodians - Hit: 26/40', followed by 'Kommandos (Choppas) ... Hit: 20/27' (40k/tools/llm_critic/runs/sweep_logs_sweep1/sweep1_03_game.log). Replay 521c0e2f shows 'Stormboyz (Kustom Choppa) -> Custodian Guard Sodality - Hit: 14/25', and the s7469/s7470 saves have _loadout_version 3 with no Stormboyz melee_loadout. So the base estimate of 8.9 is what the engine actually resolves, and the patch's '2.2 real' is wrong here. _assign_fight_attacks ranks weapons by _evaluate_melee_weapon_damage(w, _weapon_carrier_count(...)), so the patched AI would assign Choppas in these fights. Expected damage per fight against a T7 2+ Custodian Guard would drop from about 11.1 (Kommandos: Big Choppa x10 plus the gap-filled Choppas) or 8.9 (Stormboyz) to 2.2. Against Ork infantry it would drop from about 18.6 to 6.7 (Kommandos) and from 8.9 to 6.7 (Stormboyz). The change also lowers these units' threat in _estimate_incoming_melee_damage, in fight order and in the phase plan. Without CLO-CARRIER, the s7469 charge is not declined. CLO-ATTACHED alone removes +3/+5 and adds about 11-16 fight-back, and by my estimate from the logged 18.26 that leaves roughly 5-8 against the 0.29 bar.
issues.proposed_change: Remove the CLO-CARRIER branch and _wargear_names_other_weapon, and keep _weapon_carrier_count engine-faithful: narrow only where some model's resolved loadout or a wargear count names the weapon. If the Nob-weapon over-count is to be fixed, fix it in the engine first (the _melee_weapon_swingers fallback and a carriage check in FightPhase validation), then let the AI follow. Drop the test assertion that the Kustom Choppa has 1 carrier.

issues.situation: The design conflicts with the s7470 harmful guardrail and with the measured class. s7470 r2 P2 (no charge -3.50 [-5.64, -1.36], harmful) has the same structure as the s7469 finding: the same 10-model Stormboyz, 28% at Blade Champion Gamma, attached to a 3-model Custodian Guard (a 22-wound Attached unit). Its only other options are Custodian Guard Beta (the same Attached unit, 10.0 in) and Custodian Guard Gamma (10.6 in, about 8%). So under the patch every option scores about 0 and the Stormboyz skip, which is the measured worse branch. The rule depends only on the target, so it declines the whole class. I counted 15 measured Ork charges into Custodes Attached units that had a no-charge alternative; E(no charge) sums to about -6 VP (mean -0.4). The 13 of those with infantry chargers, which the patch should decline, sum to about -5. Only s7469 (+4.33) and s7470 Burna Boyz (+2.17) clearly favour declining. s7470 Stormboyz (-3.50) is harmful, and s7474 r2 (-4.25), s7468 r3 (-3.17) and s7416 r3 (-2.17) lean toward charging. In the custodes_lions list, 6 of 9 Custodes units are in Attached units, so Ork melee would stop engaging most of the army. That gives up lock-ups and objective contests in rounds 3-5, a cost that one-round rollouts cannot see.
issues.proposed_change: Do not decline charges on an Attached-unit valuation alone. At most, keep the 19.02 kill-threshold correction (no 'can halve' or 'likely kill' against 7 HP when the Attached unit has 22). Any decline gate must decline s7469 and keep s7470, s7474 r2 and s7468 r3 in a replay check before it ships. The difference between them is positional, not in the target value.

issues.situation: In the benchmark, only CLO-OVERKILL fires, and it moves charges away from near-certain kills. No unit is attached in any bench fixture: meta.formations.{1,2}.leader_attachments is {} and attached_to is null for every unit. Every melee weapon is named with a count; the bench Stormboyz carry a named 1x Power klaw, and there are no Kommandos or Beast Snagga Boyz. A Python port of both carrier versions finds 0 changed counts in mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy, mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy and asym_2000_postdeploy. So CLO-ATTACHED and CLO-CARRIER never fire. CLO-OVERKILL fixes no finding: the designer's own check leaves s7467 unchanged. I re-scored the logged charge decisions of 465 Custodes-mirror bench games (bench_data/, V0-V5 era, both seats) with the cap. It changes the chosen unit's best target 366 times: 0.4-1.4 per game, in 52% of games. Of these, 154 go from a lone Blade Champion to a full Custodian Guard squad, 70 from Prosecutors to Custodian Guard, and 62 from a wounded Allarus to Custodian Guard. In 174 of 366 the new target has lower odds. Example (ABL_heldneed_vs_V1_M1_9103, round 4): Custodian Guard Beta's 97% charge at a lone Blade Champion on an objective drops from 174.7 to 98.0 and loses to a full 20-wound Custodian Guard squad (98.04). The overkill credit was the only large term rewarding near-certain kills of characters and nearly dead units; the kill bonuses are +3/+5 against ch_damage of 2x damage. The AI would trade kills that score Assassination-type secondaries and remove OC for sticky combats with fight-back. This is the pattern of round 2's lesson. In 6 recent V9-era bench games (2 seeds) the cap changed nothing, so the V9 rate may be lower.
issues.proposed_change: Remove CLO-OVERKILL from this design, since it addresses no finding. If a cap is still wanted, exempt CHARACTER targets and targets the charge can wipe (melee_damage >= kill threshold), keeping ch_damage uncapped there, and measure it on its own over full games.

issues.situation: Coverage of the findings: the patch changes only s7469, and only through issue 1. s7467 is unchanged (the designer admits this). s7457 (Prosecutors 8% at Prosecutors, added later) is not addressed: Gun Stock keeps the whole-unit count, 0.7 damage does not reach the overkill cap, and the target is not attached.
issues.proposed_change: Report it as 0 valid fixes out of 3 findings. Do not count s7469 as fixed.

issues.situation: The Attached-unit accounting is inconsistent. The seed, gang-up and coordination blocks in _score_charge_target still use _calculate_kill_threshold(target), which is the character's 7 HP, and the uncapped damage. _evaluate_best_charge still records melee_dmg and target_hp against the character for _score_multi_target_combo, _charge_coordination and the description ('8.9 melee dmg vs 7 HP'). A second Ork charger at an attached Blade Champion still gets KILL GANG-UP +7 against 7 HP.
issues.proposed_change: Use _charge_attached_members (damage against the bodyguard, combined HP) in those blocks and in the scored_targets and coordination records.

issues.situation: The decision-change logging calls _score_charge_target twice for every (charger, target) pair, including its all-unit loops. It toggles the shared static _config_overrides mid-evaluation. When a per-player profile sets FIX_CHARGE_LOW_ODDS, the toggle is ignored, so old equals new and nothing is logged. It also compares single-target picks only, so a multi-target base pick can be logged as a change.
issues.proposed_change: Compute the previous score only under a debug flag, or pass the flag as an argument instead of mutating _config_overrides.

reviews.fires_in_bench: CLO-ATTACHED: 0, because no bench fixture contains an Attached unit (empty leader_attachments, attached_to null). CLO-CARRIER: 0, because no carrier count changes in any bench unit; the bench lists are not the critic lists (5-model Stormboyz with a named Power klaw, no Kommandos or Beast Snagga Boyz). CLO-OVERKILL: the cap binds in about half of charge evaluations. In the Custodes mirror it changes a chosen charge target about 0.2-0.7 times per game per AI seat (366 changes in 465 older bench games, both seats; 0 in 6 recent V9-era games). It never flips charge versus no charge, because it only lowers scores that were far above the bar. In the Orks mirror and in Custodes vs Orks the rate is probably similar or higher, since 5-model Stormboyz, the Mek and 3-model Warbikers are small targets for the Stompa and for Custodes damage. Most bench pairs would be identical or differ only by these re-targets, and the mechanism that changes s7469 cannot be measured in the bench.
reviews.strengths: The 19.02 reading is correct: an attached character is charged as its Attached unit, attacks go to the bodyguard first, and every member fights back. This removes a false 'likely kill' (+3/+5) from lone-character math. The fix is param-gated, and 0 restores the base behaviour exactly. The full-wounds cap was chosen deliberately so the s7431 r3 harmful guardrail still charges. The report is honest: it admits s7467 is unfixed, flags the wide reach of the carrier change, and identifies the phantom 11e overwatch penalty. The tests run on real saves, and there is decision-change logging. The design does not depend on the keeper release.
reviews.summary: Viewed through full games, this design should be dropped. (1) The one finding it changes (s7469) is flipped by CLO-CARRIER, whose premise ('8.9 estimated, 2.2 real') is false in this engine. The engine lets every eligible Stormboy swing the Kustom Choppa and every Kommando swing the Big Choppa, then gap-fills Choppas on top; logs show 40 Big Choppa attacks and 25-32 Kustom Choppa attacks. Because _assign_fight_attacks uses _weapon_carrier_count, the patched AI would pick Choppas in every Kommandos and Stormboyz fight, cutting the real damage against Custodes by about 4-5x. Without CLO-CARRIER, the s7469 charge stays far above the bar. (2) The same mechanism flips the harmful s7470 guardrail (same unit, same 22-wound Attached unit, -3.50 for no charge). The measured class of Ork charges into Custodes Attached units leans against declining (15 positions sum to about -6 VP for no charge). (3) The bench fixtures have no Attached units and no unnamed melee weapons, so CLO-ATTACHED and CLO-CARRIER never fire there. Only CLO-OVERKILL fires. It fixes no finding (s7467 unchanged, s7457 untouched) and, by my re-scoring of logged bench charges, moves charges away from near-certain kills of lone Blade Champions, Prosecutors and nearly dead units toward full Custodian Guard squads, about 0.2-0.7 times per game per seat. That is a secondary-card cost a one-round rollout cannot see. The 19.02 kill-threshold correction is the one sound piece, but it would need its own measurement and does not fire in the bench. My analysis scripts are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/rv_game_root/tools/overkill_recalc.py and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/rv_game_root/tools/carrier_sim.py. I did not run Godot (read-only), so the s7470 flip and the effect of CLO-CARRIER on fight weapon choice come from tracing the code and engine logs, not from a replay.

issues.situation: Key guardrail s7470 r2 P2 (40k/tests/rollout_cases/r4c19/20261030_160624_r4c19_00__s7470_r2_p2_charge_1_5.json). The design picks the alternative that measured worse there: no charge, E -3.50 [-5.64, -1.36] over 12 seeds. I checked this from the code and the decoded save. I did not run Godot. Every scorer input matches the s7469 finding. The Stormboyz have 10 models, a 5++ from Waaagh, no leader and no plan (player2_plan 'none'). The target is Blade Champion Gamma, attached to a 3-model Custodian Guard Sodality B: T7, 2+/4++, 22 W in total. The distance is 8.72 in against 8.49 in at s7469; both need a 9 (28%). Orks have FACTION_AGGRESSION 1.2, under the 1.5 gate, so CHARGE-COORD-SEED adds nothing. Nothing is engaged and this is the first declaration, so the focus and coordination bonuses are also 0. With the fix on, the most the positive part can reach is (2.22 dmg x 2 + CHARACTER 2.0) x trade cap 1.3 = 8.4. The fight-back costs (6.67 Custodian Guard + 3.70 Champion) x 2.0 x 0.5 = 10.4, so the value is floored to 0, the same as the report's 0.00 at s7469. The other two targets also score 0: CG B is the same Attached unit, and CG C (15 W) gives at most 5.8 against 6.67 of fight-back. The result is SKIP_CHARGE. No input of the scorer differs between s7469 and s7470, so no retuning of CLO-ATTACHED can separate the finding (+4.33) from this guardrail (-3.50). The report's guardrail table and the test do not include s7470.
issues.proposed_change: Do not ship CLO-ATTACHED (with CLO-CARRIER) as the charge_low_odds fix. If it is kept as an engine-fidelity change, add s7470 as a guard test that asserts DECLARE_CHARGE at U_BLADE_CHAMPION_C (this design would fail it). Then measure the whole class of Ork charges into attached Custodes over the existing positions (s7469, s7470 x2, s7417 r2/r3, s7438, s7468, s7437 r3) before any ship decision.

issues.situation: Only 1 of the 3 findings changes. s7467 (Allarus at a Mek, 17%) is unchanged; the report says so. s7457 (Prosecutors, 8% at a 1-model Prosecutor Squad) is also unchanged: the target is not attached, 0.7 dmg is under its 1 W so there is no cap, and Gun Stock keeps the whole-unit count because the wargear names no other melee weapon. The report does not cover s7457.
issues.proposed_change: State in the report that 2 of 3 findings stay as they are. Do not count the cluster as fixed.

issues.situation: The bench measures the wrong part. In the three postdeploy fixtures no unit is attached: attached_to is null and attached_characters is empty everywhere, and no attach step comes after deployment. So CLO-ATTACHED never fires there. CLO-CARRIER changes no count either: Stormboyz, Warbikers and Gretchin resolve through model_profiles, and Custodian Guard, Allarus, Prosecutors and Deffkoptas match their wargear names exactly. Only CLO-OVERKILL acts in the bench. It changes no finding's decision (s7467 still charges), and its full-wounds cap was chosen to keep the s7431 r3 guardrail. The bench would therefore judge the overkill cap alone.
issues.proposed_change: Give CLO-OVERKILL its own parameter. Either measure it at the existing Custodes target-choice positions before benching, or leave it out of this cluster.

issues.situation: _evaluate_best_charge recomputes the old score for every (charger, target) pair by setting _config_overrides FIX_CHARGE_LOW_ODDS to 0. This has four side effects. (a) _score_charge_target runs twice per pair in production, and all its print lines are emitted again with the old estimate, for example '[KILL-PRIORITY] Charge can likely kill Blade Champion Alpha (8.9 dmg vs 7 wounds)', plus [TRADE] and [CHARGE-COORD-SEED]. These lines appear right after the corrected scoring and mislead anyone reading the log, the critic included. (b) _note_param_read can leave FIX_CHARGE_LOW_ODDS=0.0 in the decision record's parameters_used. This happens when the old-score call is the last read, for example for chargers whose melee weapons resolve through loadouts or profiles. (c) A profile or rule override outranks _config_overrides. If the parameter comes from one of those, the 'old' score equals the new one and the decision-changed line never fires. (d) Only single-target picks are compared; the report states this.
issues.proposed_change: Remove the counterfactual. Or pass an explicit legacy flag into _score_charge_target behind a debug switch, and suppress its prints and parameter reads.

issues.situation: Not all callers use the Attached-unit view. The description string ('expected X melee dmg vs Y HP') and _evaluate_multi_target_charge still use _estimate_melee_damage(unit, target_unit), _calculate_kill_threshold(target_unit) and single-unit hits_back. A charge at an attached character therefore still reads 'vs 7 HP' while the scorer used 22 HP. A multi-target combo of a character and its own bodyguard is still counted as two targets.
issues.proposed_change: When the fix is on, take melee_dmg, target_hp and hits_back from _charge_attached_members, and skip combos whose targets belong to the same Attached unit.

issues.situation: Test gaps. The 'Choppas == 10' assertion also passes on base, because the fallback gives 10, so the plural-matching branch is never tested. The only guard, s7431 r3, is a position where CLO-ATTACHED does not apply: Blade Champion Alpha P2's bodyguard CG D P2 is wiped. That guard asserts only DECLARE_CHARGE, not the target. Several tests read state.units[...] without checking that the save loaded, so a missing save crashes the test instead of failing it. The tests do pin the fix on, erase the override at the end, fail on base for the right reasons (3 assertions) and drive _decide_charge.
issues.proposed_change: Add a plural case that base gets wrong, such as casualty scaling or a wargear count below the alive count. Assert the s7431 target. Add the s7470 guard. Guard the state loads.

issues.situation: CLO-CARRIER widens _weapon_carrier_count for every melee estimate: fight-phase weapon and target scoring at lines 18695, 18703 and 18775, and threat estimates, for both sides. The 'one carrier' rule also means that a mismatch between the wargear name and the meta.weapons name of a multi-model unit's main melee weapon now drops it to 1 carrier. That weakens the function's 'never zero a unit's output' guarantee. The rule does not fire in the bench, and it has not been measured anywhere else. Minor style point: the second 'wtype == "melee"' test is redundant because clo_carrier already requires it.
issues.proposed_change: Ship it, if at all, as a separately-parameterised fidelity change and measure it in games that use the 11e-import lists.

issues.situation: CLO-OVERKILL re-ranks Custodes charge targets. Examples of ch_damage before and after the cap: Custodian Guard into a Mek 55.6 -> 8, into 5 Stormboyz 27.8 -> 12, into a lone Blade Champion 27.8 -> 12, into Prosecutors 23 -> 8. Unit-sized targets that are not capped keep their full value, so the AI moves away from cheap kills that the secondaries pay for (risk 3 in the report). No measured position supports this.
issues.proposed_change: Measure CLO-OVERKILL alone at the existing Custodes target-choice positions before it rides along in a bench bundle.

reviews.fires_in_bench: This is an estimate from the code and the decoded fixture saves; nothing was run. CLO-ATTACHED: 0 fires. All three postdeploy fixtures (mirror_custodes_2000, mirror_orks_2000, asym_2000) have no Attached units, so every Blade Champion is a lone unit, and attachments are only made before deployment. CLO-CARRIER: 0 count changes. Single-model units return early; Stormboyz, Warbikers and Gretchin resolve through model_profiles; Custodian Guard, Allarus, Prosecutors and Deffkoptas match their wargear names exactly. So the 'one carrier' and plural rules are never reached. CLO-OVERKILL is the only active part. I approximated _estimate_melee_damage over all enemy pairs. The cap binds in about 23% of (charger, target) pairs in the Custodes mirror: Custodian Guard or Allarus into a lone Blade Champion (13.9 dmg vs 6 W) or Prosecutors (11.6 vs 4). In the Ork mirror it binds in about 10%: mostly the Stompa into small units, and Deffkoptas into Gretchin, Stormboyz or a Mek. In Custodes vs Orks it binds in about 27%: nearly every Custodes infantry charge into a Mek, Stormboyz, Gretchin, Warbikers or a Wartrike. It changes Custodes target choice in most Custodes-mirror and Custodes-vs-Orks games from round 2 on, and occasionally Stompa or Deffkopta choices in the Ork mirror. It rarely turns a charge into a skip, because capped scores still clear the low Custodes bar. Games will therefore differ, but the bench would measure only the overkill cap, which no finding supports. The parts that change s7469 never fire there.
reviews.strengths: Every changed path is gated: with FIX_CHARGE_LOW_ODDS = 0, _score_charge_target, _weapon_carrier_count and _evaluate_best_charge give the base decisions exactly. The only extra effect is a harmless param-read entry. The test also asserts the old s7469 and s7467 decisions and the old ch_damage of 26.67. The patch applies cleanly to 5e70bc2. It has no null-access or id bugs: dead characters are filtered, and a wiped bodyguard falls back to the lone unit through _attached_unit_target_id. It does not depend on the keeper release, and no debug log is removed; the decision-change line also goes to DebugLogger. The corrections it makes are true engine-fidelity fixes: an attached character is charged as its Attached unit (19.02), and a Nob's Kustom Choppa or Big Choppa no longer counts as 10 carriers. The tests pin the fix on, erase the override, fail on base for the right reasons (Kustom Choppa carriers, the s7469 charge, Mek ch_damage) and drive the real _decide_charge from saved positions. The report is honest: it admits s7467 is not fixed and lists the broad reach and the phantom 11e overwatch.
reviews.summary: The code is clean and gated, but the design cannot tell the finding from the key guardrail. In s7469 and s7470 every input to the charge scorer is the same: the same 10-model Stormboyz with a 5++, a Blade Champion attached to 3 Custodian Guard Sodality (22 W), 28% odds, no seed bonus (Ork aggression 1.2), no plan. With CLO-ATTACHED and CLO-CARRIER on, the most the positive part can reach is (4.44 + 2) x 1.3 = 8.4, against 10.4 of fight-back. Both positions are floored to 0, so the Stormboyz skip in both. Measured, skipping wins +4.33 at s7469 but loses -3.50 [-5.64, -1.36] at s7470, the key guardrail. The report and the tests do not cover s7470. The design also leaves s7467 and s7457 unchanged, so 1 of 3 findings changes. In the benchmark, CLO-ATTACHED and CLO-CARRIER can never fire: there are no Attached units, and every melee weapon resolves through profiles or exact wargear names. Only the CLO-OVERKILL cap acts, re-ranking Custodes targets in 23-27% of Custodes pairs, and it is tied to no finding. The bench would therefore judge an unrelated change. Smaller points: the old-score recomputation doubles the scoring work, re-prints misleading old-estimate log lines and can record FIX=0 in decision records; the description and multi-target paths keep the character-only view; the plural-match assertion does not discriminate from base. Verdict: drop this as the charge_low_odds fix. CLO-CARRIER is worth keeping as a separate, separately-measured fidelity fix.

issues.situation:
CH-OW-TOLL charges for an overwatch that this 11e engine never fires on a charge declaration. In 11e, Fire Overwatch (15.08) is offered only in the movement_phase_end window (StratagemManager CORE_WINDOW_STRATAGEMS). ChargePhase._after_declares_charge_windows logs "[11e 15.08] no Fire Overwatch against charging ..." and skips it. _estimate_overwatch_risk has no edition check. The cluster hint's own premise ("the cost of a failed charge is overwatch") is therefore wrong for this engine.

In the bench the trigger is the Kult of Speed Stompa. I recomputed the AI's own formula from the fixture saves (six ranged profiles, hits on 6s). Against Ork chargers in the Orks mirror it gives: Stormboyz 4.4 (25% bar 1.5), Warbikers 8.1 (bar 2.5 or 4.75), Deffkoptas 9.1 (bar 6.0), Wartrike 8.4 (bar 2.25), Wazdakka 4.4 (bar 2.5). The resulting toll is 53-78 pts, more than 0.28 x the points of every target except the Stompa.

Orks mirror, rounds 2-4: an Ork unit ends its move 8-12" from an enemy (there are no reserves in the bench fixtures). If the enemy Stompa is alive within 24" and the enemy has 1 CP or more, every long-odds charge except one at the Stompa is vetoed. Both measured Orks-mirror low-odds positions favoured charging (s7408 r3 -5.08, r2 -0.17).

Asym fixture: the same Stompa estimate (5.13 vs a full Custodian Guard's 5.00 bar, 5.5 vs a Blade Champion's 1.5, 3.4 vs Prosecutors' 1.0) vetoes Custodes long charges. That includes confident kills, because the toll is checked before the kill exemption. Example: Guard at 28% vs Stormboyz, 13.9 dmg vs 6 W, toll 55 > 0.28 x 65 = 18.

The only finding this design changes, s7467, it changes for this non-existent reason.
issues.proposed_change:
Delete CH-OW-TOLL, or gate it on GameConstants.edition < 11. If a cost for a failed charge is wanted, use the real 11e ones:
- the Command Re-roll CP the AI spends on failed 9+ rolls (evaluate_command_reroll_charge);
- CP spent on the charger's own unit_declares_charge stratagems.
Accept that s7467 is then not changed by this design: Allarus vs the Mek is a confident kill, 13.3 dmg vs 4 W.

issues.situation:
The per-target veto leaks, so the design does not do what its decision checks claim.

(a) Post-roll re-targeting at s7469, the design's own decision check. The veto removes BC Alpha (8.49") and the Stormboyz declare at Custodian Guard Delta (9.83"). Delta is BC Alpha's own bodyguard: BC Alpha's attached_to is U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_D, and RulesEngine 19.02 fights them as one Attached unit. At 11e the charge succeeds whenever any enemy is within the roll: once the declared target drops out, ChargePhase judges success on the selectable list. _select_post_roll_charge_targets then re-picks with _score_charge_target, which has no veto. CG Alpha (8.14") and BC Alpha are both within a roll of 9. So the Stormboyz still charge on every 9+ (27.8%, same as base) and hit the same Attached unit on 10+. The measured +4.33 alternative (no charge) is never played, and the report's "fewer successes (17% vs 28%)" is wrong.

The same happens at s7433 (BC Beta to its bodyguard CG Alpha, same 28%, no change in the game) and at s7470 (BC Gamma to its bodyguard CG Beta; on a 9 the re-pick goes back to BC Gamma). s7457 (+3.81) is not vetoed at all: the lone Prosecutor's fight-back is 0.22, under the 1.0 needed.

(b) Difficulty noise. The veto sets score = 0 before _apply_difficulty_noise. The bench runs at difficulty 2 (run_lanes.py: "2 = Hard (the benchmark default)"), which adds noise in -0.5..+0.5; the designer tested at Competitive. The round-2 charge bar at HARD is about 0.27-0.35 (0.85 x 0.5 x archetype / aggression). So a vetoed charge is still declared about 15-25% of the time when it is the best option left.
issues.proposed_change:
Make the veto unit-level and final:
- When a unit's best candidate is vetoed, drop every declaration of that unit whose chance to reach its nearest enemy is under 34%.
- Set vetoed candidates to -INF after noise, or skip them in the best_score pick.
- Pass the vetoed target ids to _select_post_roll_charge_targets and exclude them from the re-pick.
- Resolve attached leaders to their Attached unit (RulesEngine.attached_unit_target_id / attached_unit_models) before the single-model test and the HP and points maths.

issues.situation:
CH-LOSING-TRADE prices the fight-back at the target's full strength, although FightPhase gives the charger Fights First (charged_this_turn). The bench detachment, Lions of the Emperor, has no Custodes Fights First (that needs Emissaries). As a result, Custodes-mirror vetoes flip on list-price differences.

Bench Custodes mirror, rounds 2-4: a full 225-pt Custodian Guard (D/E/F) 8-12" from a full 215-pt Guard (A/B/C) gives removed 13.9 x 10.75 = 149 vs lost 13.9 x 11.25 = 156, so it is vetoed. The identical charge by a 215-pt unit is kept. Every Guard long charge at the Allarus is vetoed (lost 149 > removed 143).

With Fights First the target strikes back with the ~30% that survives: back about 4.2, lost about 48 (72 vs the Allarus). These are clearly winning trades. The measured Custodes-mirror low-odds positions lean towards charging: 16 positions, 11 negative, mean E -0.70 for not charging (seed-weighted -0.01). Round 2 showed that this mirror punishes holding units back.
issues.proposed_change: Compute the fight-back on survivors: back x max(0, 1 - melee_dmg / t_hp), unless the target itself has Fights First. Veto only on a clear margin (for example lost > 1.25 x removed), so that 5-10 point price differences cannot decide.

issues.situation: Rounds 3-4 are in scope without evidence. All 5 measured round-3 low-odds positions in the bench matchups favour charging (mean -2.50). Two of them are OW-TOLL vetoes: s7473 r3 -0.33 and s7404 r3 -0.42. Nothing was measured in round 4, where a successful charge onto an objective holder feeds round-4 and round-5 scoring directly (the base adds STRATEGY_LATE_CHARGE_ON_OBJ_BONUS for this).
issues.proposed_change: Limit the veto to battle round 2 or earlier until round-3 and round-4 positions are measured.

issues.situation: The phase plan does not know about the veto. _build_phase_plan flags charge_intent (score >= 3). Movement then sends the unit 70% towards that target and skips its shooting-lane planning. If the unit ends 8-12" away, the charge phase vetoes the charge (for example any Orks-mirror unit near an enemy Stompa, via OW-TOLL). The move was spent on a charge that is never declared.
issues.proposed_change: Run the unit-level veto test when building charge_intent, and drop the intent for units whose charge after moving would be vetoed.

issues.situation:
The points arithmetic is inconsistent and has a cliff:
- lost_pts uses the full meta.points when the fight-back would destroy the charger, even for a unit down to its last model.
- c_ppw uses stat W x alive models while c_hp uses current wounds. Example: s7469 Stormboyz show stat W 1 but 2-3 W boss models, giving 22 HP against 14 pts per wound.
- The cheap-charger test is a cliff. Bench Warbikers A/B (60 pts) are kept against a 125-pt Blade Champion but vetoed against the 110-pt one.
issues.proposed_change: Price losses from the remaining points (meta.points x current HP / full HP), use one wound basis for c_hp and c_ppw, and replace the 0.5 cliff with a graded points-ratio term.

issues.situation: The veto zeroes the score before the T7-11 Deadly Demise multiplier. A doomed Stompa (Deadly Demise 2D6) can therefore no longer make a long charge to explode among enemies: LOSING-TRADE sees back >= c_hp and prices the loss at 600 pts.
issues.proposed_change: Skip the veto when AIAbilityAnalyzerData.has_deadly_demise(charger) and is_unit_doomed(charger) are both true.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Fires in all three fixtures, in most games. I computed this from the fixture saves (`~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/40k/saves/*_2000_postdeploy`) with a Python re-implementation of the AI's overwatch and melee estimators. I did not run Godot, so the per-game counts are estimates.

**The bench armies are not the evidence armies.**
- Custodes: 6 Custodian Guard units of 5 models (215/225 pts), 5 Allarus, 3 Blade Champions that are not attached to anything, Prosecutors.
- Orks (Kult of Speed): Stompa, 2 Wartrikes, Wazdakka, Mek, Deffkoptas, Warbikers, Stormboyz. No Lootas, no Battlewagons.
- Every unit is deployed, so there are no reserves and no deep-strike 9" charges.

**Orks mirror.**
- CH-OW-TOLL vetoes every long-odds Ork charge at anything but the Stompa while the enemy Stompa is alive within 24" and the enemy has CP.
- CH-NO-LASTING vetoes non-confident charges at Wartrikes, Wazdakka and the Mek.
- About 1-4 decision changes per game, rounds 2-4.

**Custodes vs Orks.**
- CH-OW-TOLL vetoes long charges by Custodian Guard, Blade Champions, Prosecutors and damaged Allarus at non-Stompa targets, including confident kills.
- CH-NO-LASTING vetoes Ork charges at Blade Champions.
- CH-LOSING-TRADE vetoes Warbikers C/D, Deffkoptas and Wazdakka charging Guard or Allarus.
- About 2-5 per game.

**Custodes mirror.**
- CH-OW-TOLL never fires: Custodes overwatch estimates are at most 1.4 dmg.
- CH-LOSING-TRADE vetoes 225-pt Guard charging 215-pt Guard, and Guard charging Allarus.
- CH-NO-LASTING vetoes Blade Champion charging Blade Champion; CH-LOSING-TRADE vetoes Blade Champions charging Guard.
- About 1-3 per game.

Pairs will diverge, so the bench can see it. The real change in how often units charge is smaller than the veto count, because post-roll re-targeting keeps the charge rate and HARD noise brings back about 15-25% of round-2 vetoes. The designer's fire counts come from replays of the evidence-army cases, not the bench armies.
reviews.strengths:
- Gated by a parameter (FIX_CHARGE_LOW_ODDS; 0 gives the base exactly).
- Logs every veto ([CHARGE_LOW_ODDS]) and every kept evaluation ([CHARGE_LOW_ODDS-EVAL]), and books ch_low_odds_stake in the decision record.
- Its unit test drives _decide_charge and fails on the base.
- It changes only the charge phase, so it cannot hold units back in movement (the FAR_TRIP/OVERCOMMIT failure). A failed 11e charge does not move the unit.
- Sensible exemptions: confident kills (keeps the s7431 r3 guardrail), cheap tie-ups, round 5, and charges at 34% or better (keeps s7403).
- Independent of FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE and FIX_CHARGE_EV.
- It does fire in the bench.
- The report is candid about the s7469 and s7433 fallbacks and the overstated Stormboyz damage (the Kustom Choppa is counted on all 10 models).
reviews.summary:
Drop it.

**Why it fires in the bench.** Its main trigger there is CH-OW-TOLL, which charges an overwatch cost that does not exist in this 11e engine: Fire Overwatch fires only at the end of the opponent's Movement phase, and ChargePhase skips it. Driven by the Kult of Speed Stompa, this rule nearly bans long charges in the Orks mirror, where both measured positions favoured charging. In the Custodes vs Orks fixture it also blocks most Custodes long charges, including confident kills.

**Why the other rules don't deliver.** CH-NO-LASTING and CH-LOSING-TRADE leak in two ways. First, 11e post-roll re-targeting: a charge succeeds on any enemy within the roll, and the re-pick ignores the veto. Second, the veto is applied before HARD-difficulty noise, and HARD is the bench default. As a result:
- s7469 (+4.33) is not implemented. The fallback target is BC Alpha's own bodyguard, and the Stormboyz still charge on every 9+.
- s7433 and s7470 do not change in the game.
- s7457 (+3.81) is never vetoed.
- The only finding it changes, s7467, it changes through the non-existent overwatch cost.

CH-LOSING-TRADE also ignores the charger's Fights First. In the Custodes mirror its vetoes then turn on 10-point list-price differences, and the measured mirror data leans towards charging.

**What the evidence says.** Across 33 measured low-odds positions in the bench matchups, not charging gives no net gain: mean E -0.13 (seed-weighted +0.51, driven by the three 36-seed findings). By group:
- Custodes mirror: -0.70.
- Orks mirror: both positions favour charging.
- Round 3: all 5 positions favour charging.
- The positive evidence is confined to round-2 Custodes vs Orks, in Lootas/Battlewagon armies the bench does not contain.

**Why the idea doesn't fit 11e.** A failed charge costs at most some CP (Command Re-roll), so low odds cannot separate good charges from bad ones. The useful parts are checks on what happens if the charge succeeds: no confident kill on a single model, and a losing trade once Fights First is counted. They belong in the charge valuation at every probability (the root-cause angle), not in a veto that only applies to low-odds charges.

**If the panel revives it anyway:** delete CH-OW-TOLL, make the veto unit-level, final after noise and honoured in the post-roll re-pick, price fight-back on survivors after Fights First, and limit it to round 2 or earlier.

Very often. It should fire in essentially every bench game in all three fixtures and change a declared charge in most games. The designer's one-round replays show 3-11 vetoes of candidates scoring >= 1.0 per game (5-132 veto lines in all).

The trigger is ordinary: any positive-score charge that needs 9+ on 2D6, in rounds 1-4. That covers every charge made on the turn a unit arrives by Deep Strike (CG Delta, Allarus, Stormboyz and Tankbustas all arrive 9"+ away) and many mid-board charges. 35 of the 75 measured charge positions are such long shots by these armies.

By fixture:
- Custodes vs Orks: CH-OW-TOLL vetoes almost every long-odds Custodes charge within 24" of any of the three Lootas units when the Orks have >= 1 CP (estimate 6.8-7.6 vs Allarus or Custodian Guard). Ork charges at the three attached Blade Champions get re-labelled to the bodyguard by CH-NO-LASTING; Ork units worth under half the target's points are exempt.
- Custodes mirror: overwatch estimates are 0.2-0.4, so CH-OW-TOLL never fires. reviews.strengths:
- **Gating is exact.** Every new line is under get_param("FIX_CHARGE_LOW_ODDS") > 0.0. Param 0 gives base decisions exactly; the only trace is one extra entry in the decision record's parameters_used.
- **Low risk to the bench harness.** No RNG is consumed, so paired games diverge only where a decision changes. No debug log is removed. The veto is booked as the term ch_low_odds_stake, so the terms still sum to the score.
- **Cheap.** The cost is one extra _estimate_melee_damage per long-odds candidate.
- **Merges cleanly.** The patch applies to 5e70bc2 and on top of the round-3 keeper revision, with no dependency on the keeper release.
- **The test is well built.** It drives the real _decide_charge path, pins the override on and erases it, and its three veto checks fail on base for the right reason (the base declares the charge).
- **Some checks hold.** The exemptions work as claimed where the target really is alone (s7431 r3 and s7408, whose bodyguards are wiped). s7441 (Logan) becomes no charge, as measured (+0.94).
- **Honest report.** It flags its own weak s7469 and s7433 results and the overstated Stormboyz damage.
- **Measurable.** It fires often in the bench fixtures.
reviews.summary:
Drop. The code is clean and properly gated, but the design's effect on its findings comes from two rules facts that are wrong in this 11e engine.

1. **CH-OW-TOLL** vetoes on overwatch "paid on every declaration". At edition 11, ChargePhase never offers Fire Overwatch on a charge; it is a stratagem used at the end of the Movement phase. The 7.2 at s7467 is also about 3x inflated, because the mega-blasta is counted on all 10 Lootas. This rule alone produces the s7467 match and most bench vetoes in the Ork fixtures.

2. **CH-NO-LASTING** treats attached Blade Champions as lone models. In s7469, s7470, s7433, s7454 and s7441 each one leads a live 3-model Custodian Guard, and the fallback target is that same bodyguard. The 11e post-roll target selection still charges the vetoed leader on a roll of 9. So s7469's "fewer successes" is really only a lost Command Re-roll (need 10 instead of 9, about 41% -> 28%).

The same change hits guardrail s7470, where charging was right (-3.50): with 4 CP the base re-rolls every miss (about 48%), and the fix cannot (about 28%). The report never checked s7470. The third finding, s7457, is untouched: the fight-back is 0.22, under the 1.0 floor.

With both facts corrected (no overwatch toll, Attached units folded), none of the three findings changes. The 35 measured long-odds charges by these armies average E -0.08, so a blanket long-shot veto has no support. A new design needs a feature that separates s7469 from s7470, for example counter-charge exposure after the charger lands.

scores.note: Only design that passes the literal gates: s7467 flips to no charge, the test fails on base, and s7470 and the round-3 guardrails are untouched. But the flip comes entirely from the failed-roll overwatch term. Without it, score 1.60 clears the 1.0 bar. At 11e, ChargePhase resolves no overwatch against a declared charge: it only logs '[11e 15.08] no Fire Overwatch...', and fire_overwatch_11e exists only in movement_phase_end and never for a TITANIC unit. The base already multiplies the same score by the same phantom penalty, so the cost is counted twice. It leaves s7469 and s7457 alone (both trade up x1.3+), so it fixes 1 of 3 findings. In the bench, most of its firing comes from the TITANIC Stompa's phantom estimate (my port: 4.6-5.5 dmg against Custodes units in asym_2000_postdeploy). The rest comes from points-per-wound artifacts: UNLEASH THE LIONS duplicates the unit, so each split Allarus keeps 275 pts, and Guard is priced 225 vs 215. Its '1.0 un-lowered bar' is above the real Competitive bar (x0.7). The test pins the phantom mechanic: the with_shooter=false case is never used. The patch is small, exactly gated and cheap.

Disqualified: it vetoes the harmful guardrail s7470, and the report does not check it. The fallback CG B (10.01") needs a 10 (17%). evaluate_command_reroll_charge never re-rolls at need 10, and AIPlayer passes the declared target's distance. With P2's 4 CP, success falls from about 48% (base re-rolls every miss at need 9) to about 28%, or to a skip: toward the measured -3.50 branch. Its s7467 flip is CH-OW-TOLL, a phantom 11e cost. At s7469 the 'fallback' CG Delta is Blade Champion Alpha's own bodyguard. On a 9, ChargePhase succeeds on the selectable list and _select_post_roll_charge_targets re-picks with the unvetoed scorer, so it still charges BC Alpha and the no-charge branch is never played. s7457 is untouched (fight-back 0.22 < 1.0 floor). In the bench, most firing is OW-TOLL against the Stompa. The rest is CH-LOSING-TRADE deciding on 10-pt list-price gaps, with the charger's Fights First ignored. Rounds 3-4 are in scope with no support: all 5 measured round-3 long-odds positions favour charging. The veto is per-target and applied before noise and the Deadly Demise multiplier. Its one real plus: s7441 Logan becomes no charge (clear +0.94).

Disqualified: s7470 becomes SKIP_CHARGE, the measured -3.50 branch. Every scorer input there equals s7469: the same 10 Stormboyz with the same logged 'expected 8.9 melee dmg vs 7 HP, overwatch 0.3', 28%, and a Blade Champion attached to 3 Custodian Guard (22 W). The s7469 flip rests on CLO-CARRIER, which contradicts the engine. The Orks_2000 Stormboyz have no per-model loadout or model_profiles (I decoded the save), so RulesEngine._melee_weapon_swingers lets every eligible model swing the Kustom Choppa. The base 8.9 estimate is therefore what the engine actually resolves. CLO-CARRIER would also make _assign_fight_attacks pick Choppas in real fights. s7467 and s7457 are unchanged. The bench fixtures have no Attached units and every melee weapon is named in wargear, so only CLO-OVERKILL fires there. CLO-OVERKILL fixes no finding and draws Custodes charges from near-certain lone-character kills toward full squads (round-2 lesson risk). The decision-change log re-scores every pair by toggling the shared static _config_overrides mid-evaluation, which doubles the work and prints misleading old-estimate lines. CLO-ATTACHED (19.02) is the one sound piece and should be a separate change.

verdict.reasons:
No design is both safe and measurable, so there is no winner. I checked the claims that decide the verdict against 5e70bc2 and against decoded saves. I did not run Godot (read-only role), so the s7470 outcomes below are traced from code, as the reviewers' were.

(1) The overwatch cost is phantom. At edition >= 11, ChargePhase only logs '[11e 15.08] no Fire Overwatch against charging ...'. FIRE OVERWATCH is offered only in the movement_phase_end window, and never for a TITANIC unit. _estimate_overwatch_risk has no edition, TITANIC or engagement check, and the base already multiplies every charge score by its penalty. Narrow's only flip (s7467) needs the (1-p) x 7.2 term: 1.60 clears its 1.0 bar without it. Game's s7467 flip is CH-OW-TOLL. In the bench the term is set mainly by the Kult of Speed Stompa, a TITANIC unit, so both designs would mostly measure a Stompa-proximity rule. The evidence came from Lootas lists and never tested that.

(2) The finding s7469 and the harmful guardrail s7470 have identical target-side inputs. Root floors both to 0 and skips s7470. Game cuts s7470's success from about 48% to about 28% (or skips it). Both are therefore disqualified. The decoded saves show what does separate the two positions. At s7469 the Stormboyz are alone (only Battlewagon A within 9"), with two Custodes Attached units within 10". At s7470 they stand inside six other Ork units, all within 2.6", and face one Attached unit.

(3) Leaks and fidelity problems. Post-roll re-targeting undoes per-target vetoes. Root's carrier change contradicts the engine's own melee resolution. The bench has no Attached units, no reserves and only named melee weapons.

(4) No design changes s7457. Each design changes at most one finding soundly or not at all.

Narrow ranks first only because it passes the literal gates and is small and exactly gated.

Corrections to the reviews:
- s7469 has first_turn_player 2, so P1's round-2 charge phase follows P2's. Narrow's fire count there is possible.
- ai_versions.py run defaults to Competitive (score noise 0). Game's pre-noise veto leak therefore affects Hard and Normal player games, not the bench.

A sound fix would need four things:
(a) A separate, separately benched rules-fidelity change that removes charge-time overwatch from _estimate_overwatch_risk at 11e. It makes charges more likely, so measure it alone first.
(b) A term that differs between s7469 and s7470:
- friendly melee units that can also charge the target this phase;
- enemy units that can Heroically Intervene or counter-charge after the charger lands;
- the real 11e costs of a successful charge: an engaged unit cannot Fire Overwatch or Heroically Intervene next turn, it loses its Shooting phase, and the AI spends CP on re-rolls.
(c) A test of the declaration side effect first. With FIX_CHARGE_EV off, a failed declaration still feeds KILL GANG-UP and pile-on bonuses to later chargers. At 8% odds, s7457's +3.81 is too large to come from the Prosecutors' own charge outcome.
(d) Proof that the fix fires on the three bench fixtures for the same reason it fires at the findings.
required_changes: Resubmission prerequisite (no winner this round): do not use overwatch as a charge cost at edition >= 11. Delete narrow's lo_fail_ow term and game's CH-OW-TOLL, or gate both on GameConstants.edition < 11. Rebuild the s7467-shape tests so they do not depend on a ranged unit within 24" plus defender CP.

Make any veto unit-level and final. Pass vetoed target ids into _select_post_roll_charge_targets and exclude them from the re-pick. Apply the veto after _apply_difficulty_noise and the T7-11 Deadly Demise multiplier, or skip the candidate with `continue`. Resolve leaders and bodyguards with _attached_unit_target_id, so one veto covers the whole Attached unit and the multi-target combos built from it.

Keep the AI damage model faithful to the engine. Do not narrow _weapon_carrier_count's melee fallback unless RulesEngine._melee_weapon_swingers and FightPhase validation change in the same commit: Orks_2000 Stormboyz and Kommandos have no per-model loadout, so the engine lets every eligible model swing the Nob weapon. Drop CLO-OVERKILL from this cluster; it addresses no finding.

Add real-save guard tests using root's .w40ksave harness. s7470 r2 P2 must DECLARE_CHARGE with U_BLADE_CHAMPION_C among its targets, with the 4-CP need-9 re-roll path intact. s7469 (U_STORMBOYZ_A), s7467 (U_ALLARUS_CUSTODIANS_A) and s7457 (U_PROSECUTORS_A_P2) must SKIP_CHARGE for that unit. s7431 r3 and s7403 r3 must still charge their logged targets.

Key the cost on features that differ between s7469 and s7470: friendly melee units able to charge the same target this phase, and enemy units able to Heroically Intervene or counter-charge the charger after it lands. Price only real 11e costs of a successful charge: no Fire Overwatch or Heroic Intervention next turn while engaged, no next Shooting phase, CP spent on charge re-rolls. Limit the rule to battle round 2 or earlier until round-3 and round-4 positions are measured.
grafts: root CLO-ATTACHED (19.02): value a charge at an attached leader as a fight with the whole Attached unit (combined kill threshold, damage on the bodyguard first, fight-back from every member). Ship it as its own parameter and extend it to the CHARGE-COORD gang-up block and the description and multi-target paths. Measure it on critic-list games, because the bench fixtures have no attachments.
root's test harness: decode the rollout-case .w40ksave and drive _decide_charge with the real DECLARE_CHARGE list. It is the right way to pin s7469, s7470 and s7457.
narrow's booking pattern: book the drop as a ch_* term so the terms still sum to the score, and let a 0-score target add 0 to the _score_multi_target_combo EV. Keep its round gate as a safety limit.

game's s7441 result (Logan Grimnar 28% at an attached Blade Champion becomes no charge, measured clear +0.94): keep it as a guard test for the next design. Reuse its structured {veto, reason, terms} helper, but log once per (charger, target) per phase.

FIX_CHARGE_EV (already in code, OFF since the round-1 bundle, whose difference was not significant): its CH-ARRIVED rule stops a failed low-odds declaration from feeding KILL GANG-UP and pile-on bonuses to later chargers. Re-test it as the candidate cause for this cluster before writing new charge logic.
extra_checks: Replay s7469 r2 P2, s7457 r2 P2, s7467 r2 P1 and s7470 r2 P2 over 36 seeds with FIX_CHARGE_EV=1 vs 0 on V9R. This tests whether the declaration's side effect (gang-up bonus for later chargers after a failed roll) drives the measured loss; an 8% charge measuring +3.81 at s7457 cannot be explained by its own outcome.

Bench a separate rules-fidelity change on its own: _estimate_overwatch_risk returns 0 for charge declarations at edition >= 11, or at least skips TITANIC and engaged shooters and counts real carriers. Measure it alone, because it makes charges more frequent, before any cluster fix is stacked on it.

For any resubmission, count [CHARGE_LOW_ODDS] fires per game on mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy, mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy and asym_2000_postdeploy. Attribute each fire to its trigger: Stompa proximity, the UNLEASH THE LIONS split (each Allarus model keeps meta.points 275), or the 215/225-pt Guard price gap.
Drive APPLY_CHARGE_MOVE at s7469 with the veto in place: declare CG Delta and force a roll of 9. Confirm the post-roll re-pick no longer charges Blade Champion Alpha.
Check s7470 with P2 at 4 CP. Assert that both the declaration (Blade Champion Gamma, need 9) and the Command Re-roll decision are unchanged.

Full-game check for the round-2 lesson: paired, side-swapped bench of V9R vs V9R plus the candidate on all 3 fixtures, reporting secondary VP separately from primary VP and the count of changed charge declarations per game.
verdict.merge_risk: Nothing is merged; V9R stays as it is. If narrow were merged anyway, it would apply cleanly as one gated block in _evaluate_best_charge, but its whole effect rests on the phantom overwatch estimate. A later fidelity fix to _estimate_overwatch_risk would silently turn it into a no-op and make its test fail. Root has the highest merge risk. It edits _weapon_carrier_count, which also drives fight-phase weapon choice and threat estimates for both sides, and _score_charge_target, which the post-roll re-pick also calls. It also toggles the shared static _config_overrides during evaluation. Game adds a third per-target veto path in the same block that other round-4 charge fixes edit. Its log volume (up to 132 veto lines per game) would also crowd the critic's input.
